state.package: fortify-paid-verification (Kogen Intent). Its scenarios describe the verification controller this Intent SHIPS (the Candidate's code). That controller is proved by offline ExUnit tests in the Candidate and by the paid target live-shape-to-build, whose test rsyncs the Candidate into a fixture and runs `mix kogen.build` there, which compiles and runs the Candidate's new controller against a nested fixture Intent.
state.self_hosting: This Build itself is run by MAIN's controller (the code loaded at Build start). Main settles from the Stop hook's v1 path (KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT supplied by main), byte-freezes the Makefile and priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml, requires check.sh in preflight, parses Reviewer verdicts with exact keys, and only checks proof selectors for existence. The package deliberately keeps the Stop v1 path working, leaves Makefile/catalog unchanged (not in guarded paths), keeps the catalog `check` target, and only the no-context Stop mode is removed (main never uses it; main always supplies a v1 context). New features such as catalog_changes.add, proof.base, and the ledger are switched on only for LATER Builds run under the new controller; this Build's own contract uses none of them (legacy contracts stay valid, labelled unproven-on-base). The ledger verdict field is required only when a ledger is supplied, and main supplies none.
state.approval: The Shaper explicitly approved this package's 12 scenarios, including the README/prompt policy scenarios offline-first-target-selection and self-hosting-two-step-guidance, and two paid targets for two edited live owners.
state.known_limits: Risk integrity-limits already records that until the follow-up switches integrity on, Kogen's own Builds rely on Review against empty or weakened proof tests. references.yaml runtime paths exist in the main checkout (ignored files not present in the audit clone). evidence/investigation.md is a historical note written for an earlier seven-scenario revision.

controller-owns-verification.given: A Build started under the new controller, on any configured route (including the hybrid routes from cross-harness-adversarial-roles), whose Developer turn has just ended. The Stop registration still exists, but no v1 context is supplied.

proof.paid_reason: provider-required: live-shape-to-build; observation: a real Claude Code Developer (on main's default route, which after cross-harness-adversarial-roles pairs it with a real Codex Reviewer) ends a turn with the Stop hook inactive, receives the controller's failed verification through a resume of the same session, fixes it, and a later controller verification passes before real Review and commit; offline-limit: a fake harness cannot show that a real model session acts on a controller resume message or that the real CLI accepts the inactive Stop hook

controller-owns-verification.then: The parent controller, running the trusted code the Build started with, computes the Candidate id itself (a private-index git write-tree, refusing assume-unchanged and skip-worktree entries). It runs `make check`, then the selected targets in catalog order, as child processes outside the Developer process tree. It re-checks the Candidate id after each target; a mutation fails the cycle. It writes the only context, state and history files, and no Developer-launched process gets their paths or `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT`. It is also the only writer of the local Verification Record and its history (`Kogen.Check.record_path/0`, `Kogen.Check.history_path/0`). After each cycle it writes them in today's line format (candidate, status, target, exit_code, session_id, attempt_token, finished_at), and it archives and resets them only at each outer attempt, as today. The record's `target` field keeps the constant `check` as a format value for existing readers; it selects nothing. So the unedited live-reviewer-rework owner and its support files (`test/kogen/live_reviewer_rework_test.exs`, `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`, `test/support/live_rework_audit.ex`) keep working, and this Intent leaves them byte-identical, because it doesn't run that target. This holds even when the controller itself inherited one: for example, a nested `mix kogen.build` started by a target under main's Stop runner inherits the outer v1 context. The new controller explicitly removes `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` from every Developer, Reviewer and target child environment. That way a nested fixture's Stop hook can't write to the outer Build's state. The Stop hook does nothing. Handoff, Jev and Review read only this controller settlement. A complete Build through the new controller shows a failed-then-passed controller verification across a resume of the same Developer session, followed by Review and commit.

same-intent-catalog-change.given: An approved Intent whose `intent.yaml` declares `catalog_changes.add` with new target names. Its guarded paths cover the Makefile and catalog, and a scenario selects one added target. (This is a later Intent, or a fixture Intent in this Intent's tests, built under this Intent's controller. This Build itself changes neither the Makefile nor the catalog, because main's controller byte-freezes the catalog.)

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: catalog comparison and failure routing run through the controller with real Make targets in a fixture repository; no provider semantics

same-intent-catalog-change.then: The catalog is no longer byte-frozen after admission. At admission, `verified_by` may name a declared added target. It is rejected when it names an undeclared unknown target, or when `add` names a target that already exists. Each cycle, the controller reads the Candidate's catalog and Makefile only as data; it never loads Candidate code. Every selected target must exist in both. Every added target must meet every catalog rule (unique rank, dependencies, owner, and a rehearsal when provider-backed). A scenario that selects an added provider-backed target lists that target's rehearsal test as a file selector, so `controller-runs-proof-selectors` covers it. Removing, renaming or editing unselected targets needs no declaration; it appears in the verification-surface ledger. A missing or invalid selected target is a verification failure that resumes the same Developer. It doesn't stop the Build. The trust anchor for each rule is the admission catalog, never the Candidate's.

no-special-gate-target.given: A repository whose Makefile and catalog declare offline and provider-backed Make targets under any names. For example, an offline `test` target with no dependencies and no `check` target at all. The approved scenarios each list their targets in `verified_by`. (This is a fixture repository built under this Intent's controller. Kogen's own Makefile and catalog keep `check` unchanged in this Build, because main's controller runs it.)

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: plan loading, target selection and guard naming are pure controller logic exercised through Kogen.Build with a fake harness; no provider semantics

no-special-gate-target.then: No target name is special; Make stays the only runner. Admission no longer requires a `check` target. The plan loader accepts a scenario's `verified_by` when all of these hold: it is a nonempty list of distinct catalog targets; it contains at least one `provider_backed: false` target and at most one `provider_backed: true` target, which must equal `proof.paid_target`; every listed target's `dependencies` are also listed; and the list follows catalog rank order. The Build runs exactly the union of the approved `verified_by` lists, in rank order, and never silently adds a target. Receipts form one uniform list, with no separate `check` field in the tracking record, handoff report or review packet. The Bash gate guard blocks `make <goal>` for every catalog target, not a hardcoded `check`/`live` pair. The catalog validator requires at least one offline target with no dependencies, instead of `check`. This repository's existing contracts (`[check]` and `[check, <paid>]`, including this Intent's own) still validate unchanged. Maintained prompts and docs describe `verified_by` as the complete, explicit list.

controller-runs-proof-selectors.given: An admission catalog that declares `verification_surface` (`tests` and `runner` globs), `focused_runner` (an argv template with `{paths}`) and `base_cache` (paths to copy). A contract whose scenarios carry the new `proof.base` field: `fail` for new or changed behaviour, `pass` for preservation.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: the controller runs real focused tests in a fixture project against a real git-archive base; no provider semantics

controller-runs-proof-selectors.then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

verification-surface-ledger.given: A Candidate that changes, adds, deletes or renames files matching the admission catalog's `verification_surface` globs, including paths outside every scenario's `affected_paths`.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: ledger computation, verdict schema enforcement and routing are controller logic exercised with a fake Reviewer; no provider semantics

verification-surface-ledger.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

stop-route-bootstrap-only.given: The Candidate after this Build, with the Stop scripts still registered in `priv/kogen/claude_code/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json`.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: stop_hook drives the real scripts in both context cases with a counting fake target; the inactive path prints the same {"continue":true} the real CLIs already accept

stop-route-bootstrap-only.then: (a) It prints `{"continue":true}`, runs no Make target, and writes no verification record, state, history or log. (b) It behaves exactly as today's unified protocol, so the older controller can settle, review and commit this Build automatically. `Makefile` and `priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml` stay byte-identical to main, because main's controller stops a Build whose catalog changed after admission. `live-native` stays in the catalog unchanged. The target split belongs to the follow-up verification Intent.
